data.note: counts above ~3.75e9 inflated by host int64 overflow; examples listed are below that threshold and valid

evidence.summary: Reciprocal constants (MULT=2454267027=ceil(2^34/7), SHIFT=34) compute floor(v/7) incorrectly starting at the legal uint32 value 3435973841 (computed q=490853406 vs true 490853405), with mismatches repeating every 7 thereafter. Overflow caveat: the total count is unreliable above v≈3.75e9 due to signed int64 wrap in the host check, but the first mismatch examples are below that threshold and are exact, and a quotient overestimate by 1 also forces col out of [0,6]. This matches GPU behavior (see t9).

rationale: Reciprocal division with a single precomputed multiplier and shift is only exact on a bounded value range; the shift/multiplier choice (_SHIFT=34, ceil multiplier) must be proven to cover all 2^32 inputs, and an off-by-one in the constant bounds silently corrupts row/col for large indices.

scope_evidence.summary: EVERY unsigned 32-bit value is legal, 0 through 4294967295, and every coordinate must equal the integer mathematical target EXACTLY; any division method is allowed only if it satisfies this for every legal index.

scope_rationale: The contract requires exact row=floor(idx/7) and col=idx-7*row for every uint32 value; a quotient error at any legal index violates the exactness requirement.
statement: The reciprocal-multiplication constants (MULTIPLIER=ceil(2^34/7), SHIFT=34) fail to compute floor(value/7) exactly for some legal uint32 values, producing wrong row/col coordinates.

evidence.summary: End-to-end GPU comparison run() vs reference(): exact for tiny boundary lists and N=1, but false for N=255, 256, 257, 4093, 131072 and contiguous offset views — make_inputs random uint32 values above ~3435973841 (0.8*2^32) produce wrong row (and thus col) coordinates, violating the exactness requirement for legal indices. Input tensor itself was preserved.

rationale: run() with masked loads/stores and fresh output allocation is straightforward, but a runtime comparison on representative N values (including extremes 0, 4294967295, and various N sizes) is needed to confirm end-to-end behavior matches reference exactly.

scope_evidence.summary: Return a fresh uint32 [N,2] tensor on indices.device with columns [row,col]; every col in [0,6] and 7*row+col equals the original index exactly; 1<=N<=131072.

scope_rationale: The contract requires the returned tensor to be a fresh [N,2] uint32 with exact coordinates for N in [1,131072]; run() must satisfy this on admitted inputs.
statement: The Triton kernel's end-to-end run() output differs from reference() for some admitted inputs (e.g. boundary values 0, 4294967295, or particular N sizes).
